summary.overview: Paperplane has clear project rules, focused parser tests, and CI gates, but the reviewed Codex window could not consistently connect the final change to a runnable check, attributable failure diagnostics, and revision-bound acceptance.

dimensions.label: Task Understanding
dimensions.summary: Project rules identify the product boundary and canonical code routes, while task-level acceptance remains only partly reviewable.

dimensions.label: Controlled Execution
dimensions.summary: Pinned dependencies and commands exist, but the managed environment blocked the focused parser check before pytest started.

dimensions.label: Change Validation
dimensions.summary: Focused tests cover normal parser decisions, but final-change linkage, failure correlation, and one central recovery branch remain unresolved.

dimensions.label: Reliable Delivery
dimensions.summary: CI workflows are present, but the bounded evidence contained no revision-bound acceptance, approval, rollback, or recovery result.

dimensions.label: Learning Capture
dimensions.summary: The bounded review detected possible repeated validation friction but could not establish a stable procedure, durable owner, or later comparable outcome.

findings.title: The managed environment blocks focused parser checks
findings.reason: The project exposes a focused parser test, but the reviewed run never reached pytest because dependency synchronization tried to repair Torch, found missing package metadata, and then could not replace a locked DLL. This leaves agents without the intended fast validation signal until the project-owned environment route can diagnose or isolate that state.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add the smallest project-owned doctor or isolated verification route that detects an unusable managed environment before dependency synchronization and gives a safe recovery path without deleting an active environment.

## Validation

- Run the new diagnostic against the observed broken-environment condition
- Run the documented isolated route and confirm `tests/test_parser.py` reaches pytest
- Confirm the route does not stop or overwrite an unrelated running process
expectedOutput: Provide one supported diagnostic and isolation route that either starts the focused parser check or reports the exact lock and safe recovery boundary.

findings.title: Failed document parses cannot be correlated with the promised logs
findings.reason: The batch runtime converts unexpected parse exceptions into a message that directs the operator to local logs, but the inspected runtime and parser owners expose neither a discoverable log sink nor a request identifier that survives into the error result. A failed hybrid parse therefore cannot be joined from trigger through decision and failure to its returned outcome.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Give the unexpected parse path one privacy-safe correlation identifier and an owned local diagnostic sink, then return that identifier with the sanitized error outcome. Keep uploaded content and model output out of logs.

## Validation

- Add a focused test that forces an unexpected parser exception
- Confirm the returned failure and local diagnostic record share the same identifier
- Confirm the diagnostic record contains no document bytes, extracted text, prompt content, or secret values
expectedOutput: Make one failed parse traceable across the runtime boundary without weakening Paperplane's local privacy contract.

findings.title: Hybrid parser fallback can change without a focused regression failure
findings.reason: The parser decides whether a page-processor exception fails the document or preserves available local blocks, but the inspected focused parser suite covers successful strategy and threshold decisions only. A regression in this recovery branch could silently change a usable fallback into a failed document, or the reverse.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Add focused parser tests for the page-processor exception branch, covering both preservation of available local output and failure when no valid fallback exists. Keep production behavior unchanged unless a test exposes a contract mismatch.

## Validation

- Run the new recovery tests in `tests/test_parser.py`
- Run the full focused parser test file
- Confirm both recovery outcomes assert the returned warning or exception contract
expectedOutput: Protect both sides of the hybrid fallback decision with deterministic regression tests.

findings.title: Recent task handoffs do not retain final-change verification
findings.reason: Three reviewed Codex implementation episodes reached handoff with checks near the final edits, but none retained a reviewed link between the final change set and a relevant passing check; one retained a post-change lint failure. This does not prove the changes were wrong, but it prevents the harness from establishing validated closure.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness fix this issue

Extend the existing project validation guidance so a coding-agent handoff records the final revision, the smallest relevant project-owned checks run after the last edit, and each result. Reuse the commands already owned by CI and the project manifest.

## Validation

- Exercise the guidance on one bounded code change
- Confirm the handoff names the final revision and post-edit check results
- Confirm a failing final check blocks a successful-completion claim
expectedOutput: Make final-state verification reviewable without requiring raw session or command transcripts.

findings.title: The reviewed window cannot classify recurring implementation friction
findings.reason: The bounded Codex review found several plan-to-change-to-check handoffs with execution friction, but root and check portfolios were truncated and no final-change-relevant check was reviewed. The evidence cannot decide whether this is a stable reusable procedure, normal task complexity, or unrelated local failures, so Learning Capture has neither a clean no-candidate result nor a supported durable owner.
findings.aiFixPrompt:
/better-harness review these sessions

Run one bounded, privacy-safe outcome review for the emitted implementation candidates. Classify task family, final outcome, friction owner, verification boundary, and whether at least two independent episodes share a stable trigger, ordered stages, and stop condition. Do not create a Skill, Memory, Hook, or workflow unless that comparison supports one and existing coverage has been checked first.

## Validation

- Produce a complete recurrence decision for the displayed candidates
- Preserve provider labels and omission counts
- Return `defer` or `no candidate` when independence or outcome evidence remains insufficient
expectedOutput: Resolve the current recurrence evidence gap without exposing raw prompts, session identifiers, or private paths.
